newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: PNG governor general urges troops back to barracks.
newsitem.headline: PNG governor general urges troops back to barracks.

text.p: Papua New Guinea Governor General Sir Wiwa Korowi on Wednesday appealed to soldiers to return to barracks and for people not to take to the streets and "destroy the nation" as pressure mounted on Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan to resign over a mercenary deal.

"No matter what amount of evil we think they have committed, your confrontation directly with the parliament and its members will not help and I appeal to the Papua New Guinea Defence Force as your commander in chief to move back to barracks this morning," he said in a national radio address.

"Let us not take to the streets to destroy the nation," Korowi said. Chan has not been seen in public since Tuesday evening after he survived a parliamentary motion calling him to stand aside pending an inquiry into the hiring of 70 African mercenaries to end an uprising on the island of Bougainville.
About 80 heavily armed soldiers and thousands of anti-government protestors beseiged the parliament building overnight preventing politicans from leaving.
However, Chan as well as Deputy Prime Minister Chris Haiveta and Defence Minister Mathias Ijape were whisked away by police immediately after the vote.
Local media reported that Chan would conduct a cabinet meeting by telephone later on Wednesday and there was specuation that the cabinet would put more pressure on him to stand aside.
